activity: Ted Horrobin chatting with Ted Baldwin at Edge End Colliery in the Forest of Dean.

te.text:
STEPHENS/CARDIFF.              D.H.                2.12.56
THERE'S COAL IN THEM THAR WOODS.
In the Forest of Dean, Gloucestershire, there are
several large coal mines, and also small private levels,
worked by handfuls of men.
One of these is the Edge End Colliery, near Coleford,
where five men work.     One of these miners is Ted
Horrobin, who has spent many years underground.   But
now he drives the haulage engine at the top of the
colliery level, and cuts and shapes pit props in the
forest clearing outside the level.    Running past there
is the main Monmouth-Gloucester road, and probably
most of the people who pass think that Ted is a forestry
worker.   But the wood that he cuts so skilfully is 
nearly all imported.
OPS.   Ted Horrobin chatting with one of his friends,
75-years-old Ted Baldwin, who spent 53 years working in
the Forest minexs.    With Mr. Baldwin is his dog Spot.

activity: Bakers and Master Bakers judging bread at a baking competition at Caxton Hall.

te.text:
By BARBARA MATTHEWS
IT WAS a magnificent bloomer, with a beautifully symmetrical crust and a crum that surpassed them all for its sheen, its even holes, its bluish tint and its superb aromatic flavour.
And it won the British Baker silver challenge shield, the bakery trade's most important trophy, at the Caxton Hall in London yesterday.
Mr. Sidney Geary, of Valley Bakeries, Ratby, Leics, carried off the shield on behalf of his son and partner, Charles, who actually baked the loaf.
Competition was fierce amongst different shaped loaves - bloomers, tins, farmhouses - and, in other categories of the contest, between hand-raised pork pies, Easter cakes with flop-eared bunnies, and scenes from Swan Lake, painted in confectioners' colours.
A loaf may seem a simple object beside these, but its judging was a complex ritual of prodding, stroking and sniffing (or, as bakers put it, testing the aromatic flavour).
Judges were looking for the sheen, the bluish tint a correctly-fermented loaf should possess, and the holes that prove there was still life in the dough.
"That is the way to make a loaf properly white," Mr. Geary told me. "Not bleaching the flour."
Mr. Geary's firm, three generations of bakers who supply about 150 Leicester shops, is what the trade considers a "small" baker. "We make our bread the old-fashioned way, although with modern equipment," he said.
"This loaf was baked on the oven bottom, and we managed to bring the dough to the peak of fermentation. It was a test of skill."

"PASSING OUT" - AS A COOPER - ANCIENT APPRENTICE
CEREMONY IN PIMLICO...  1-9-50.

Twenty two year old RONALD BARHAM of
South Lambeth - today became a qualified COOPER at
the end of his six and a half years apprenticeship..

at the Watney Brewery, Pimlico, in which BARHAM was
placed in the first barrel of his own making - and
fellow coopers enjoyed themselves by pouring various
concontions - including oily soot - over him - rolled

health and skill as a new Cooper was toasted by all
present..

    The finest specimen of cutlery in England, if not
the world - a 75-blade Norfolk Knife - was sold at Sotheby's
today for £2,500.   It was made specially for the 1851
exhibition at the Crystal Palace in Hyde Park by Joseph
Rodgers & Son of Sheffield - one of the oldest cutlery firms
in the world.   It was bought by a Mr. Rogers and will be
on permanent lean to the Cutlers Company.

KEYSTONE PHOTO SHOWS:-   The Norfolk Knife pictured at
             Sotheby's today where it was sold for £2,500.
             H/keystone           IS/820467

meet the orders now pouring in from all parts of the
world. The Standard Eight is a four door, four light,
clean line, four-seater saloon, steel panelled, rust-
proofed and dustproofed. A substantial parcel shelf
is available in the facia panel and there is a capacious
luggage boot at the rear, access to it being from the
rear compartment of the car - the rear seat squabs
folding forward. It has an overall length of 11ft.
10in., width of 4ft. 10in. and a height (unladen) of

PROPERTY OF
DAILY HERALD
RCD. 27 JUN 1950
PLEASE RETURN
TO
ART LIBRARY

200359 AND
PRINCESS AT A CHRISTENING

Mersham,Kent,Eng; Princess Elizabeth, who is
expecting her second baby this summer, attended a
christening ceremony in the tiny church here as a
godmother. The baby christened, five-weeks old
Michael John Ulick, is the second son of Lord
and Lady Brabourne.

husband play for the local team in a cricket match.

Louis Philip Knatchbull, has the Duke of Edinburgh
as a godfather.

she attended the chistening of Lord and Lady
Brabourne's child, five-weeks old Michael, at Mersham
church.

te.text:
MANUFACTURING THE "FULLY FASHIONED".
NYLON HOSE IN THE MAKING.

British womenfolk are eagerly awaiting the
arrival in the shops of the supplies of Nylon hose -
items to bring a little luxury to the austerity ridden
legs of Britain. Stocking manufacturers throughout the
country are experimenting, calculating costs and planning
to produce sufficient quantities of stockings made of this
all wonderful, but mysterious material known as 'Nylon'.
Eventually Nylon stockings will be remarkably cheaply
produced, but initially it is expected that they will cost
about 15/- a pair, for 'fully fashioned' and about 8/11
for the 'semi' variety.

KEYSTONE PHOTO SHOWS: Miss Emily Claxton, is a "looper".
This entails sewing up the soles of the stocking without
leaving a seam. The job needs nine months experience
for real efficiency. Photograph taken at a British
Stocking factory.

ROPER                                   16.3.39

50 to 100,000 FULLY BOUND BOOKS PER WEEK.
Some of the largest Perfector printing
machines in Europe:  Printing 64 pages on
each side of the sheet.
The copy from the author goes to Linotype
machines - they have a keyboard similar to
that of a typewriter - which transforms the
printed word into metal type.  The type is
made up into a page form which has a 
facsimile taken off it in paper flong,
from which the metal cast is produced.
Plates are assembled in special order on the
bed of the printing machine and after the
application of ink, the printed sheet is
produced.
The printed sheet goes through nearly half-
a dozen operations such as folding, gathering,
sowing and cutting, when it is transformed
into the bound copy sold to the public.
Real leather is used for the making of cases.
Real 22 carat gold is applied to the lettering.
Someofzsthe
Above is one of the machines used in the
Coplax process.  Its object is to produce
the concave front, and the convex back and
hinge.
OPS.

te.text:
STEPHENS.         D.H.           23.1.56
LANDSLIDE AT TAFF MERTHYR COLLIERY, TRELEWIS, GLAM.
The railway lines which used to carry more than 1000 tons
of coal per day down the valley from the Taff 
Merthyr Colliery, Trelewis, were swept away in a 
landslide a week ago. Workmen are now busy driving
a way through the mass of sodden earth.
O.P.S. Standing on the mud, with the railway lines 
buried deep below, the colliery manager Mr.William 
Hart * talks to Peter Williams from the colliery 
washery (left) and Tom Wardman, an N.C.B.platelayer, 
who have been cutting channels in the mud to drawn 
away surface water.

activity: design and manufacture of pre-cast concrete embrasures for sandbagged blockhouses

te.text:
B EMBRASURES FOR SANDBAGGED BUILT BLOCKHOUSES.
The weak feature in all rapidly constructed blockhouses
is the wooden framing used to form the opening.  The
opening does not protect the rifleman because the rim
can be penetrated by a bullet, also the splintered wood
carried away by the bullet can produce nasty wounds.
The present suggestion is to pre-cast the embrasure
opening of the desired aperture and angle, the outer
extremity having a light sheet steel framing embedded
in the face to prevent the concrete edges shattered by
a bullet from being detached and forming missiles.
The embrasure weighs less than 1½ cwt. and can easily
be lifted into place by two men.   Manufacture can be
made in quite simple wooden moulds by any local building
contractor, breeze block manufacturer, in Corporation
yards, and so on;  using the quick setting concrete
and be produced ready for installation within 24 hours.

An American Church has ordered three 21-foot stained-
glass windows from Britain's oldest firm of glassmakers.

been commissioned by St. Bernard's Church, Mount Lebanon,
Pennsylvania, from the Whitefriars Studios, of Messrs.

CROWN COPYRIGHT RESERVED. MINISTRY OF HOUSING & LOCAL GOVERNMENT.
Four prototype houses built for the Sheffield City Council by the
Public Works Department under the 5M system of construction devised
by the Research and Development Group of the Ministry of Housing
and Local Government. This system, which marks a new attempt to
bring the advantages of industrialisation into the field of house-
building, has been derived from the 5M CLASP system used at
Stevenage for a group of old people's flatlets. The new system
is called 5M, because as at Stevenage, it is based upon a planning
grid of 1' 8" (5 x the module of 4"). The object has been to
modify the CLASP system, which has been shown to have advantages in
the reduction of site labour and building time, to suit the
performance standards, and the levels of cost, of 2-storey housing.

activity: Princess Anne launching the tanker Esso Northumbria at Wallsend on the River Tyne.

te.text:
Seconds after the launch the huge bulk of the Esso Northumbria makes the Tyne at Wallsend look like a ditch.
Not bad for a starter
PRINCESS ANNE launched her first ship yesterday with all the aplomb of a veteran.
She pulled a lever, sent a bottle of champagne crashing against the Esso Northumbria's bows, and the monster tanker slid smoothly into the river Tyne.
It was a faultless launch. The quarter-million-ton tanker, the biggest ever built in Britain, did not touch the opposite bank.
The ship made the Tyne at Wallsend look like a ditch. The tanker is 280ft. longer than the QE2, big enough to hide Buckingham Palace behind.
After the bottle-smashing, 40 seconds ticked away before the huge ship, towering above the Princess like a 10-storey building, started to move down the slipway.
As the ship gathered momentum and ploughed into the water, raising clouds of steam and dust, 10,000 people roared their approval.
The £6 1/2 million ship is the first of four ordered by Esso in Britain and was launched on time.
Afterwards Princess Anne, who was presented with a diamond brooch by the shipowners, said: "I have had the honour of launching the largest ship ever built in this country—and for a starter, that is not bad.
"I have experienced the warmth of a Tyneside welcome which has been overwhelming—two things I shall never forget."
Sir John Hunter, chairman of Swan Hunter, yesterday confirmed that the shipyard have won an order for another quarter-million-ton tanker from Anglomar Shipping of London, as reported in yesterday's Sun.
By FRANK DAWES
Shipping Correspondent

PROPERTY
- 3 MAY 1969
Please return to Art Dept.

te.text:
The bungalow at Felpham, near Bognor, which

BOGNOR, Sussex,
Tuesday.
A PRETTY FAIR-HAIRED
YOUNG WOMAN AND
THREE MEN ARE BEING
HUNTED TO-NIGHT BY
SCOTLAND YARD AND THE
POLICE OF ALL THE HOME
COUNTIES.
Hearing that they were living
in a bungalow at Felpham, near
here, and wanting to question
them concerning an epidemic
of burglaries, the police last
night threw a cordon round
their little home.
From their hiding places, the
officers saw, at 2 a.m., one of the men
walking near the bungalow.
They chased him to a car, but were
seconds too late. The car sped off in the
darkness.
The watchers' attention thus diverted,
the woman and the two other men
jumped into another car and made off.
These two cars were both high-powered
saloons.
In a few minutes a police net was
thrown across roads all over Surrey and
Sussex. Messages were flashed to every
police station between the coast and
London.
Level crossings were closed. Cars were
stopped and searched.
But this was not enough to hold the
suspects. At Arundel a car broke
through a police cordon at 70 miles an
hour, and a constable had to jump for
his life.
Near Horsham one car defied three
police challenges.
By now wireless messages had been
sent from Scotland Yard to squad cars
all over the London area giving descrip-
tions of the four people. They were also
circulated by teleprinter to all stations.
One of the suspected cars has been
found abandoned at Arundel, another at
Kingston, after a chase by police along
the by-pass almost into the town.

AERTIST'S IMPRESSION OF THE VAST ANGLO-IRANIAN
SCOTTISH GRANGEMOUTH REFINERY...   28-12-51

Scottish Oils Ltd.. - a member Company
of the Anglo-Iranian Company Group, was formed in 1919
to bring under unified management the Scottish shale-
oil industry which it still controls today.. It owns
twelve shale-pits, four shale retorting works and a
refinery at Pumpherston, Midlothian, where shale-oil
and natural petroleum from Anglo-Iranian's oilfield
at Eakring, Nottinghamshire, are processed.. Grangemouth
Refinery was opened in 1924 with a capacity for
360,000 tons of crude oil a year.. It was temporarily
closed during the war - and work resumed in 1946 - and
has rapidly expanded until it now covers 350 acres and
has a production of 2,250,000 tons per annum..

KEYSTONE PHOTO SHOWS:-  An artists impression made in

A GIANT air-sea rescue operation
was in full swing last night after
the 5,600-ton oil-drilling rig, Sea
Gem, with 30 men on her platform, had
collapsed in the icy North Sea.
Flares were dropped by aircraft as an armada
of ships searched the wreckage-strewn sea for
survivors from the ill-fated rig 40 miles off
Grimsby.
Late last night three men were known to be
dead and another seven were missing. Of the 20
known survivors, three are seriously injured.
Two bodies were taken aboard rescue ships. A
third man died in a
helicopter which was
taking him to hospital.
Sea Gem, which was
being used by British
Petroleum to probe the
seabed for gas, capsized
mysteriously yesterday
afternoon.
